sources.title: Khaleej Times: Hackers target supermarket freezers as Europe moves to prevent further attacks
Brussels Signal: France accuses Iran's Revolutionary Guards over fridge attacks
n0n group claims attack on Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan

categories.summary: Suspected Iran-linked hackers keep targeting supermarket refrigeration and small water systems in Europe and the US; France has blamed Iran, others have not formally. A ransomware gang called n0n claims it hacked Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan through a supplier; this is unconfirmed and no card disruption is reported. The collector grouped this and the Microsoft outage with a 'China campaign', but the Microsoft outage was a software bug and the Visa claim is from a criminal gang, so that link looks wrong. Google reports Russian hackers used AI to run a largely automated attack. Nothing reported in Australia; our banks, phones and grid are normal.

drivers: Suspected Iranian hackers keep hitting supermarket freezers in Europe and small water systems in the US, and are probing flaws in Copeland refrigeration controllers. If deliberate, the aim is to hit back over the Gulf war by disrupting allies' everyday services; next targets could include cold storage and water in countries like Australia, ports, and bank websites. This is a hypothesis: only France has formally blamed Iran.

A run of big outages overseas (US flights, Microsoft, Chase, Apple) were faults, not proven hacks. A ransomware gang now claims it hacked Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan through a supplier; that is unconfirmed.

summary: Oil fell about 5% overnight after President Trump signalled restraint on Iran, but Hormuz is still effectively shut by the US blockade standoff, so fuel stays dear. Suspected Iran-linked hackers are still going after refrigeration and water systems in Europe and the US; nothing has hit Australia. A ransomware gang claims it hacked Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan through a supplier; this is a claim, not confirmed, and card payments here are normal. Locally there are no fire bans or CFS warnings near home, and the grid and phone networks are normal.
